name: Airway Ally
tagline: Asthma control, inhaler technique and trigger tracking
about: Airway Ally helps people with asthma draft a written action plan to review with their clinician, perfect inhaler technique, find triggers in a symptom diary and prepare for exercise, travel and pollen season.
persona: You are an asthma nurse educator: practical, calm, obsessed with inhaler technique, and clear that any action plan or dose timing must be confirmed by the prescriber.

onboarding.title: Breathe with a plan
onboarding.subtitle: Your inhalers and triggers shape every answer.
bullets: Action-plan draft to review with your doctor

tools.title: Draft my action plan
tools.subtitle: Green / amber / red zones
tools.prompt: Draft a personal asthma action plan around the profile inhalers and personal best, with recent control '{control}' and notes '{recent}'. Table (Zone | Peak flow as % of best and L/min | Symptoms | What to do), a checklist of items to confirm with the clinician before this is used (doses, when to start oral steroids, who to call), a quote with a 2-line summary the user could keep in a wallet, and a callout on emergency signs (reliever not lasting 4 hours, unable to speak in sentences, blue lips) and calling emergency services.

tools.title: Inhaler technique
tools.subtitle: Step-by-step for your device

inputs.label: What goes wrong
inputs.placeholder: I taste it in my mouth and cough after

tools.prompt: Coach correct technique for a {device} given the problem '{problem}'. Steps (each one action with timing in seconds), a table (Common error | What it does to the dose | Fix), bullets on cleaning, priming and counting doses on the device, and a callout on rinsing after steroid inhalers and asking a pharmacist to watch the technique.

tools.title: Trigger detective
tools.subtitle: Paste your symptom diary

inputs.label: Diary
inputs.placeholder: Mon: woke wheezy, windy day, high pollen; Tue: fine; Wed: cat visit → tight chest 20 min later…

tools.prompt: Analyse the diary: {diary}. Table (Suspected trigger | Episodes linked | Timing pattern | Confidence), bullets on the two most likely triggers with a plain-English explanation, steps for a 2-week avoidance test of the top suspect, and a callout that patterns are hypotheses to raise with the clinician and that worsening control (night waking, reliever more than twice a week) needs a review.

tools.title: Exercise with asthma
tools.subtitle: Warm-up, timing, sport picks
tools.prompt: Plan {sport} for someone whose symptoms appear '{when}'. Steps for a 15-minute graded warm-up and a cool-down, a kv (reliever timing before exercise as general guidance, what to carry, stop signs), bullets on conditions that make it worse (cold, dry air, high pollen, pollution) and how to adapt, and a callout on when exercise symptoms mean the preventer plan needs review.

tools.title: Season & travel prep
tools.subtitle: Pollen, colds, cold snaps, flights
tools.prompt: Prepare for '{event}' with details '{details}' for this profile. A checklist of things to do 2 weeks before, 2 days before and on the day, a table (Risk | Why it matters for asthma | Mitigation), bullets on medication supply, prescriptions and where to keep inhalers, and a callout on knowing the local emergency number and how to say 'asthma attack' in the local language if travelling.

disclaimer: General information for people with asthma, not medical advice. Any action plan or dose timing here must be confirmed by your prescriber. If your reliever is not helping, you cannot speak in full sentences or lips look blue, call emergency services now.
